newsitem.title: UK: Med oil products mixed on lazy trading day.
newsitem.headline: Med oil products mixed on lazy trading day.

text.p: Mediterranean oil products were mixed on Thursday, with gasoline supported and gas oil and fuel steady to weaker traders said.

Tight supplies and light buying interest from Italy and the eastern Med continued to support gasoline. There was little chance of fresh supplies from NWE with the market there looking equally tight and arbitrage elswhere more attractive.

Eurograde cargoes talked in a steady but slightly wider range around $217-$220 per tonne cif Med. Despite the tightness one trader house was reported to have booked a vessel for 29,500 tonnes for early June shipment to Argentina.
Naphtha prices held steady around $174/$177 a tonne cif Med but trade was thin with buyers scarce.
Gas oil remained fragile although some traders said an Indian Oil Corp (IOC) tender for some 850,000 tonnes of mainly high speed diesel for July delivery might firm the market.
Other were more sceptical and unsure material would be sourced from the Med.
Russian cargoes were valued around June IPE -$5.50 cif NWE, while Italian islands 0.2 percent material was assessed at around quotes fob hi +$1.0/+$2.0.

High sulphur fuel markets were thin with good Russian availability again the major factor. A distressed cargo of good quality M100 straight-run was heard to have eventually found a home in the Italian bunker market at low numbers.
Nothing else was seen on the water but the "Purple Star" loading Odessa June 5-10 was on offer.
A Tunisian spot tender to swap high sulphur cracked for low sulphur was heard won by a Wall Street trading house.
Syria tendered to sell two 50,000 tonne cargoes of good quality high sulphur fuel. Loading dates were June 15-20 and 25-30 and bids were due by Monday.
